messages:
marta: Heads up — noticed a cluster of ephemeral nodes (ephemeral-pool-3) with very high metadata IOPS and pods hanging on graceful termination. evictions are timing out and kubelet stuck on unlink.
infra-cleaner-bot: cleanup-job/ephemeral-prune started on node ip-10-2-45-18 at 2026-03-17T11:12:03Z
marta: Kernel logs from one of the nodes show repeated nvme errors and ext4 complaints. pasting the snippets I grabbed:

marta: ```
Mar 17 11:13:02 ip-10-2-45-18 kernel: nvme0: pci 0000:5e:00.0: Namespace 1: pblk failed to read metadata
Mar 17 11:13:02 ip-10-2-45-18 kernel: blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456789
Mar 17 11:13:02 ip-10-2-45-18 kernel: ext4 warning: delayed inode table write failed
``` 

devon: Can you paste iostat and nvme-cli smart logs? wondering whether this is raw device-level wear/slow path or just GC/compaction spikes.
samir: iostat and nvme-cli from same host:

samir: ```
$ iostat -xz 1 3
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  rrqm/s  wrqm/s  r_await  w_await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1         1200    950   102400  51200     0      0     9.3      12.7    0.80  98.7

$ sudo nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0
critical_warning: 0
temperature: 39 C
data_units_read: 12345
data_units_written: 672345
host_reads: 987654
host_writes: 234567
available_spare: 12%
percentage_used: 78%
``` 

devon: percentage_used at 78% and available_spare 12% — drive is pretty worn. but the pattern looks like metadata-heavy tiny writes. overlayfs + container churn and the cleaner job together are amplifying metadata IO.

marta: The cleaner runs every 5m and deletes millions of small files under /tmp/ephemeral/* after pods exit. That matches the timing of the I/O spikes.

ops-oncall: Short-term: I cordon'ed one node and set a taint to stop scheduling, started a drain with --delete-local-data for pods that can't move. Would it help to throttle the cleaner or change its batch size?
samir: Yes. Immediate mitigations:
- throttle cleaner: add a sleep between deletes or use ionice -c3
- switch cleaner to delete in larger batches but pause fsyncs (careful)
- mount overlay with nfs-like options? (not ideal)
- schedule fstrim more frequently so controller GC has room

devon: Also can change kubelet eviction grace to give more time to unlink, but that's just papering over the root cause.

marta: Filed INF-472 to track this (replacement + long-term change). Proposal in ticket:
- reduce cleaner concurrency and add ionice
- increase fstrim cadence to hourly for ephemeral pools
- add a health-check that looks at nvme percentage_used and available_spare to auto-cordon at 85% used
- roll nodes more gradually and replace drives hitting warranty threshold

infra-cleaner-bot: cleanup-job/ephemeral-prune completed on ip-10-2-45-18 (exit 0) duration 00:00:32

devon: Cost tradeoffs: replacing drives early vs doubling ephemeral pool to spread write amplification. Replacing now has capex / warranty calls; doubling pool increases infra spend but reduces wear rate per-disk. leaning toward targeted replacements + cleaner tuning.

ops-oncall: For this maintenance window (Sat 02:00 UTC) I'll coordinate a rolling reimage of ephemeral-pool-3 with one node out at a time. Will add ionice and reduce cleaner concurrency in config before bring-back.

marta: Thanks. Also add alert for ext4 errors and nvme percentage_used delta > 5% in 24h. If anything spikes overnight ping oncall.

devon: quick config we changed for cleaner (example):

devon: ```bash
# new cleanup wrapper
ionice -c3 /usr/local/bin/ephemeral-prune --batch-size=2000 --sleep-ms=200
```

marta: I'll update INF-472 with the plan and assign owners. ping me if you see a new ext4 warning.
ops-oncall: noted, will monitor and post updates here. :thumbsup:
